findings.title: Inventory does not enforce the authorized public companion-code and database scope before reads
findings.evidence: inventory() adds every file found under the ignored phase1_research_copilot tree and every research/*/public_archive.sqlite match; neither is a finite reviewed allowlist. denied() rejects selected names and suffixes but not phase1_research_copilot/config/credentials.json. An in-memory inventory probe returned that synthetic credential path and research/not-approved/public_archive.sqlite. denied() returned false for the credential path, and screened_reason() returned null for its synthetic JSON api_token value. build() therefore reaches read_regular() and can persist such content rather than excluding the credential path before opening it.
findings.impact: The current invocation can read and copy ignored operational or credential material outside the promised public companion-code scope. A public_archive.sqlite basename alone does not bind selection to the four authorized public databases. This is an authorization-boundary failure, not a demand for universal secret detection.
findings.actual_repository_exposure: UNVERIFIED: no real inventory or private configuration was inspected, and no actual credential presence is asserted.
findings.minimum_required_change: Bind ignored companion additions and database additions to explicit reviewed public paths, and refuse credential/runtime candidates before read_regular(). Preserve ordinary authorized repository files; do not silently expand scope from directory membership or a database basename.
findings.proof_required: Synthetic inventory tests must exclude a non-allowlisted companion credentials file and a fifth public_archive.sqlite path. A read spy must prove refused paths are never opened, while the approved public source and exact database paths remain selectable.

findings.title: Extension-only archive dispatch permits a nested denied path to bypass screening
findings.evidence: The same synthetic uncompressed TAR containing a .env member returned archive_member_refused when named bundle.tar but returned null when named bundle.txt. TAR headers and the synthetic payload decode as UTF-8, so the generic text branch accepts the container without inspecting its members. An included outer file can therefore carry a nested path the archive branch would reject.
findings.impact: Nested archive and secret-path exclusions are bypassable by a harmless outer rename. UTF-8 decodability is not sufficient evidence that a file is plain text, and the plan's bounded recursive inspection claim does not hold for this supported container under an alternate suffix.
findings.actual_repository_exposure: UNVERIFIED: no real renamed archive was searched for or inspected.
findings.minimum_required_change: Recognize supported archive containers independently of their outer suffix, or conservatively exclude container-like non-text content before the generic text acceptance path. Keep the existing recursive limits and member-path denial; no broader scanning framework is required.
findings.proof_required: Add a synthetic renamed-TAR regression proving its .env member is refused regardless of outer suffix, plus a safe plain-text control and a safe supported archive control.

shown_controls.claim: Source reads use descriptor-relative O_NOFOLLOW on each component, require a bounded regular file, and compare file metadata around the read. Leaf and ancestor symlink fixtures are excluded.

Recognized archive suffixes receive recursive byte/member checks, limits, duplicate/path checks, and link refusal; restoration accepts only expected regular-file members with matching sizes and hashes.

shown_controls.claim: Destination creation is exclusive and outside the resolved source root under a canonical existing parent. Existing and in-repository destinations are rejected by synthetic tests.

shown_controls.claim: The helper contains source reads and destination writes, not source deletion, Git mutation commands, credential configuration, account actions, service startup, or market-data analysis. Its Git inventory subprocess uses git --no-optional-locks ls-files.
shown_controls.limit: Static command/write-surface review, not actual-copy filesystem tracing; source credential reads remain a blocker under RC-01.

shown_controls.claim: Synthetic fixtures demonstrate preserved selected bytes and executable mode, source-change refusal, journal deferral, and readonly immutable quick_check of a restored .sqlite copy.
shown_controls.limit: This is local selected-file proof only. The code quick_checks .sqlite restored files, not every .db file that inventory could admit.
